config.text: The mechanics: standard error = %%0%% (how much sample means wobble), stretched by %%1%% for 95% confidence — the 68–95–99.7 rule inverted. Halving the width takes four times the data.
config.hint: One is a ratio with a square root in the denominator; the other is the two-sided 2.5% point of the normal curve.

activities.caption: one line of the variance recipe is wrong — click it
activities.name: ciVarSpot

config.prompt: One line of this SD recipe is wrong — click it:
lines: Deliveries of 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 minutes: the mean is 8, deviations are −4, −2, 0, 2, 4.
Sample variance = 40 ÷ 5 = 8, since averaging five numbers divides by five.
For roughly bell-shaped data, about 95% of values sit within two SDs of the mean.
config.correction: For a sample, divide by n − 1 = 4: variance = 40 ÷ 4 = 10, which is what line 4's square root assumes — the degrees-of-freedom correction.
config.why: Squaring punishes large misses, which is why one wild delivery inflates the SD while the median and IQR barely move.

activities.anchor: a larger poll does not make commutes more alike
activities.caption: two spreads, one square root — drag the divider
activities.name: ciSpreadCompare

config.prompt: The hinge between spread of data and spread of estimates — drag the divider:

before.label: spread of the data
before.text: the individuals' standard deviation — whatever n you collect, people still vary this much; no sample size changes it

after.label: spread of the estimate
after.text: the mean's standard error, s/√n — the wobble of averages, which the square-root law does shrink

config.why: More data steadies the estimate, not the population — that distinction is what separates description from inference.

activities.caption: file each question with its measure
activities.name: ciChooseSort

config.prompt: Nine houses at £200,000, one at £2,000,000 — and four other jobs. Which measure fits?

items.label: incomes, house prices, hospital stays — skewed
'total taxable wealth' — every house counts, extremes included
'what does a house cost here' — the typical house
instantly computable, destroyed by a single outlier

config.why: The mean (£380,000) and its SD answer the wealth question; the median (£200,000) and IQR answer the village question — neither is wrong, and justifying the choice is the skill.

activities.anchor: the statistical bargain of the age
activities.caption: call the wobble's shrinkage
activities.name: ciWobbleEst

config.prompt: Double the sample size. The standard error falls to what percentage of its old value?
config.why: 1/√2 ≈ 0.71 — quadruple n and the wobble halves. Averaging adds independent errors, variances add, so the mean's SD is σ/√n.
config.context: That single line of algebra is why polls of 1,000 work at all.

config.q: Same data, but you report a 99% interval instead of 95%. What happens?
choices: It narrows — extra confidence sharpens the estimate
It widens — 2.576 SEs instead of 1.96 — and can become too fuzzy to act on
Same width, just labelled more confidently
config.why: Confidence is bought with width, so the same data delivers a vaguer statement. The level is a design choice matched to the stakes, not a virtue to maximise.

activities.anchor: Planning in advance is the professional move
activities.caption: price the half-width in commuters
activities.name: ciPlanEst

config.prompt: Sample SD s = 8 minutes. What total n does the recipe demand for a half-width of ±2 minutes?
config.why: (1.96 × 8 ÷ 2)² ≈ 62 — and roughly 250 to quarter it. Decide the width you can live with, then solve for n and budget accordingly.
config.context: Precision is sold at a square-root price: 100 commuters bought ±1.57.

activities.caption: the grouped walk, end to end
activities.name: ciWalkOrder

config.prompt: Sixty delivery times in four classes — order the quartile walk:
items: Cumulative counts across the classes: 8, then 30, then 48
Q1 = the 15th value (60 ÷ 4) sits in the 20–30 class — 8 values lie below it, so walk to the 7th of the class's 22
Q3: the 45th value lies in the 30–40 class, 15 of its 18 values in — Q3 ≈ 30 + (15 ÷ 18) × 10 ≈ 38.3 minutes
IQR ≈ 15.1 minutes — carrying the uniform-spread assumption that individual data would not need
config.why: The estimate assumes values spread evenly inside each class — one reason statistical agencies publish grouped summaries and, where privacy allows, microdata.
